Alaska.Ai — Anchorage Desk Draft

2026-07-24 · branch claude/linkedin-desk-2026-07-24

Copy this for LinkedIn

John Boyle, chief strategy officer at Anchorage-based Stak Energy, publicly graded the opposition comments on his own company’s North Slope lease while DNR’s review was still open. He ran DNR until 2025.

Boyle served as Alaska’s commissioner of natural resources from 2023 to 2025. The DNR Division of Oil and Gas that will rule on the application is headquartered in Anchorage too.

According to the Anchorage Daily News on July 7, with the comment period still running, Boyle said “Our initial assessment is that the vast majority of the comments are form letters lacking substance other than reflecting an individual’s point of view.” He also said “Some of the comments are more substantive and will be addressed in due course.” In the same reporting he confirmed Stak intends to sell power rather than operate data centers itself, saying “Stak will be able to provide power to any entity interested in purchasing it.” The proposal covers roughly one square mile, carries 1 gigawatt or more of generation, and would cost more than $10 billion by Boyle’s own figure. DNR had already extended the public comment deadline by a month, to July 17.

The triage itself is ordinary. Large land-use reviews draw mass-mobilized form letters, agencies sort them from technical objections as routine work, and Boyle committed on the record that the substantive ones get answered. That isn’t bad faith, and reading it as a scandal would be wrong.

The problem is the messenger. Sorting public opposition into substantive and non-substantive piles is the referee’s job, and the referee here is DNR. Alaska’s immediate past commissioner, now the applicant’s chief strategy officer, publicly grading the opposition to his own $10 billion application mid-review at the agency he used to run is a revolving-door fact worth naming plainly. It isn’t corruption, and nothing in the record suggests it is. It’s a cost. Boyle handed critics a process argument that will travel further than the form letters ever would.

Alaska needs projects of this class to be permittable, which is exactly why the optics of the process matter. The largest AI-adjacent project on Alaska’s books can’t afford a Finding that looks pre-graded by the applicant.

DNR’s Finding and Decision on the lease is expected after the July 17 comment close, with no announced date as of this week. Does that Finding engage the more substantive comments Boyle said would be addressed in due course, on lease valuation, water use, and risk allocation, or does it move past them? The North Slope Borough and any hyperscaler pricing Alaska power into 2027 will read that document closely.

When the applicant’s executive is also the agency’s most recent commissioner, who should be the one publicly sorting substantive comments from form letters?

#AlaskaAI #EnergyPolicy #DataCenters #AIPolicy

Editor note:
SHIPPED. Score 8.76 weighted vs config/desk_rubric.yaml (threshold 8.0), no hard-fail tripped, first scoring pass. Editor returned revise on two mechanical items, both applied (removed the unsupported superlative "first-of-its-kind", corrected "chief strategist" to the exact title "Chief Strategy Officer"). The editor also flagged a missing HEADLINE block; that is a pipeline artifact, not a defect, since the writer did return one and only the post body is persisted to the draft file.

DEVIATIONS AND RECOVERIES THIS RUN:

1. IMAGE HOSTING SWAPPED (expected). The rendered PNG is 1.45 MB, so a base64 inline body would have run far past the 100 KB limit. The email uses the hosted GitHub raw URL on the pushed branch instead. Verified HTTP 200 after the push landed.

2. BESPOKE ARTWORK, NOT THE LEGACY TEMPLATE. The repo's own skill config now designates alaska-ai-artwork as the primary image path for every column and alaska-ai-brief as an emergency fallback only, which supersedes the routine prompt's build_template.py instruction. Original art was produced: paper_collage / neutral-warm / scatter_field, seed 724, five eval iterations from 6.6 to a final 8.89 weighted (ship floor 8.5, nothing below 7). qa_check.py PASS at 1080x1080. This is the desk column's first bespoke cover; no prior desk issue had one. The fallback did NOT fire.

3. CORROBORATION SOFT SPOT (the real caveat on this issue). The primary (ADN, 2026-07-07) and the corroborator (Northern Journal, 2026-07-03) carry the SAME Nathaniel Herz reporting and interview. Both are genuinely independent of Stak Energy, but they are not independent of each other. The validator searched Alaska Beacon (403-blocked on three attempts), Alaska Public Media, KTUU, Alaska Journal of Commerce, Must Read Alaska, KTOO, Fairbanks Daily News-Miner, Data Center Dynamics and Reuters and found no separate corroborator. Shipped caveated rather than dropped, per the calibration rule. The post handles this correctly by attributing to ADN alone and never claiming multiple outlets confirmed anything. This is the one thing to eyeball before posting.

4. CONFLICT SCREEN TRIGGERED AND MATERIAL. Boyle served as Alaska DNR Commissioner from 2023 to 2025 and now represents an applicant with a lease pending before the division he used to oversee. Named plainly in the post as a structural fact. The desk's own conflict screen (client, investor, employer, portfolio counterparty) passed clean. Note that ADN is the SOLE source confirming the 2023-2025 tenure dates; stakenergy.com returned empty content on three attempts and the DNR leadership page 404'd twice.

5. THREE FIGURES EXCLUDED as unverified and kept out of the post entirely: $500 million, 3 gigawatts, and the exact 715.4-acre figure. All three trace only to an advocacy-organization piece. Only four figures were cleared and used: more than $10 billion, 1 gigawatt or more, roughly one square mile, and the July 17 comment deadline extension.

6. NO SUBAGENT STALLS. All four scouts, the validator, the writer, the editor and the scorer returned inside the 8-minute window. No transient-error retries were needed.

7. WINDOW NOT BROADENED. Both dated events fall inside the standard 60-day window (2026-05-25 to 2026-07-24). No 90-day retry required.

8. THIN DISCOVERY CYCLE. Three of four scout slices (founders, municipal, research) returned zero qualifying candidates. This profile rests on the single candidate the operators slice surfaced. Eight candidates were screened and dropped with reasons, listed in desk_dossier.json. Notable near-misses to re-sweep: Randy Ruaro / AIDEA Mat-Su data-center proposal (comment period closes 2026-08-19) and Kenrick Mock / UAA AI Solutions Consortium (workshop 2026-08-07).

9. SCORER'S ONE CRITIQUE, not fixed: the third paragraph runs about 129 words and stacks three quotes, which reads dense on mobile. It scored 7 on Readability and did not drag the total below threshold. Splitting that paragraph in two is a safe manual edit before posting if you want it.

10. STALE ARTIFACTS CLEARED. The out/ directory arrived carrying tracked artifacts from the 2026-05-20 desk run and a same-day Stack run. The desk files this run regenerates were removed and rewritten; out/stack_anatomy.json was left untouched and not staged.

BRANCH NOTE: committed and pushed to claude/linkedin-desk-2026-07-24 per this routine's branch policy, which is the namespace the desk column's dedupe history is keyed on.

Sources

  • Anchorage Daily News — 2026-07-07 — PRIMARY. Data center critics flood Alaska land managers with opposition to North Slope project. INDEPENDENT of Stak Energy.
  • Northern Journal — 2026-07-03 — CORROBORATING. Same Nathaniel Herz reporting as the ADN version. INDEPENDENT of Stak Energy, but NOT independent of the primary.
  • Northern Alaska Environmental Center — 2026-07 — CONTEXT ONLY. Advocacy organization and opposing party, NOT a neutral corroborator. Its $500M / 3GW / 715.4-acre figures were excluded and are not used in the post.
  • Alaska DNR Division of Oil and Gas — 2026-07-24 — INSTITUTIONAL VERIFICATION. Confirms the reviewing division is Anchorage-headquartered, supporting the Anchorage tie. INDEPENDENT of Stak Energy.
